label: Multiplayer Sync
title: Multiplayer sync
lead: KrokMP compatibility: automatic sync for registered content, plus a host-authoritative snapshot and message API.
bodyHtml:
Wait, what?

CUCoreLib has a soft compatibility layer for KrokoshaCasualtiesMP (KrokMP, the multiplayer mod). Soft means literal: with KrokMP not installed, none of it loads and singleplayer is untouched.

Two separate things live behind that layer.

  • Content — custom items, buildings, tiles and liquids you registered through CUCoreLib resolve over KrokMP's own object sync, so a peer can spawn your content from the same string ID it already sends on the wire.
  • State — CUCoreLib runs its own host-authoritative snapshot on top of KrokMP's transport, plus a request and message API for your traffic.

For registered content and registry-backed state you write no multiplayer code at all. Everything below is the part you drive yourself: CUCoreLib.Networking.MultiplayerApi.

Supported KrokMP versions

CUCoreLib supports KrokMP 4.0.1 and 4.1.2. It does not branch on the version: every KrokMP symbol it needs is resolved by name, so the same CUCoreLib build runs unmodified on either one. KrokMP 3.x is not supported, and that is deliberate — the v3 backfill was deleted rather than kept alive.

That said, 4.0.1 and 4.1.2 cannot connect to each other. KrokMP changed its item/building sync bit layout and its Steam transport framing between those builds, so a mixed lobby desyncs inside KrokMP and will look exactly like a CUCoreLib bug. Keep every peer on the same KrokMP version.

How state moves

KrokMP is host-authoritative, and so is CUCoreLib's sync layer: the host owns the truth, clients pull it, and clients never broadcast.

  • A connecting client requests the full snapshot once (cucorelib.sync.snapshot) and applies every module in it. If it lands while the client is not in a world, CUCoreLib caches it and replays it once you are in one.
  • The host can push a fresh snapshot to everyone with BroadcastSnapshot when the shape of the shared state changes.
  • Custom statuses ride their own channel and are polled once a second per client; the host answers with that client's body, so one player's poison never lands on another player.
  • Your traffic shares the same envelope: JSON, gzipped, base64'd, then framed onto KrokMP's message channel. Up to 60 000 characters ride as a single write; larger payloads are split into segments and reassembled, with a hard 16 MiB ceiling per message.

Sprites are deduplicated across a capture pass, so a manifest that uses the same texture in fifty items costs one copy. A module that throws is logged and skipped, on both capture and apply, so one broken mod cannot take the whole snapshot down — if your state arrives half empty, search the log for multiplayer snapshot capture failed for module.

What you get for free

CUCoreLib registers its built-in snapshot modules during startup. Anything you put through the normal registries is already covered.

Module keyWhat crosses the wire
itemsCustom item definitions: names, descriptions, category, sprites, wearable flags, weight and condition behaviour.
liquidsCustom liquid definitions: colour, value per litre, injection and usability flags, crafting qualities.
lootpoolsLoot pool contents and weights, so world loot matches the host.
tilesCustom block definitions. Re-injected into the live world array after every module runs, so custom indices cannot briefly fall back to vanilla tiles.
liquidtilesLiquid tile definitions.
buildingsCustom building entity definitions.
moodlesCustom moodle definitions.
settingsRegistered mod options and their values.

Statuses are not in that list on purpose: they are per-player, so they sync over their own channel instead of the shared snapshot.

ItemRegistry.Register("conicalFlask", flaskInfo, flaskSprite);
// This will automatically have multiplayer support, alongside most custom fields ^
BuildingEntityRegistry.Register("SporeMine", new CustomBuildingEntityDefinition
{
    Name = "Spore mine",
    Sprite = sporeMineSprite,
    Components = new[] { typeof(SporeMineScript) }
}); // Every peer gets a spore mine. Its SporeMineScript logic is yours, and is not synced.

What is not free: your own MonoBehaviour logic, state you keep outside the registries, and anything you change after a peer pulled its snapshot. Those need a sync module or a message, below.

The one hard requirement

Stable string IDs on every machine. The snapshot carries data, not behaviour: when a peer applies it, CUCoreLib keeps whatever the local registry already had (your useAction, SpawnComponents, sounds) and takes the plain fields from the host. A peer that has your mod therefore keeps its logic; a peer that does not still gets the right name, description and sprite, and a prefab it can spawn — minus your scripts.

Prefabs resolve locally. When KrokMP asks for KMPSR_<youritemid>, CUCoreLib answers from its own registries and hands over the instantiated object, so no asset has to travel out of band.

Terrain is the one place where indices rather than IDs cross the wire, and KrokMP's world chunks are one byte per tile: custom tile indices must stay inside 36-255, or registration warns and ignores the tile.

Messages and requests

The public surface is CUCoreLib.Networking.MultiplayerApi, so a dependent mod never has to reflect into KrokMP internals. Use messages for live actions, and snapshots for durable state.

Payloads arrive as a JToken, and every send returns false instead of throwing when the bridge is not there. Channels are plain strings, compared case-sensitively, so namespace them (mymod.kiln.setmode) rather than inventing a bare mode.

APIUse it for
IsAvailableWhether the CUCoreLib bridge found KrokMP and installed its receivers. False with no KrokMP, or on a build whose signatures it could not match.
IsRunning, IsClient, IsServer, IsHostRole checks before server-only or client-only work.
KrokMpVersionThe installed KrokMP version, or null when it is not loaded. For logging and diagnostics — CUCoreLib never gates on it, and neither should you.
RegisterServerHandlerClient-to-server traffic. Return a JToken to answer a request, or null for fire-and-forget events.
RegisterClientHandlerServer-to-client events.
RegisterHandlerThe same one-way handler on clients and the server, no response.
SendToServerClient one-way event to the host.
RequestServerClient request with a response callback.
SendToClientServer event to one client ID.
BroadcastServer event to every client. The host is skipped unless includeHost: true.
SendToPeerSends to the chosen client when called on the server, and to the server when called on a client. It never relays between clients — that is what host Broadcast is for.
RegisterSyncModuleYour own durable state inside the shared snapshot.
CaptureSnapshot, ApplySnapshotBuild or consume a snapshot by hand, mostly for tools and testing.
BroadcastSnapshotHost push of the current full snapshot to every client.
RequestInitialSnapshotClient re-pull, when something changed that only otherwise lands on join.
GetCustomPlayerData, GetCustomPlayerLimbDataServer-side read of one player's custom body or limb statuses.
RequestCustomPlayerData, RequestCustomPlayerLimbDataThe same, from a client.
ResolveKrokMpType, FindKrokMpMemberKrokMP types and members by any name they have ever used. See When KrokMP renames something.

reliable: false sends unreliably, which means it is cheap and can quietly never arrive. Use it for chatter you resend anyway, and leave everything that matters on the default.

Registration is startup-only: multiplayer channels and sync modules are deliberately excluded from strict content reload, so register them from Awake like any other registry rather than from a reload path.

These APIs may be lacking, apologies. If something you need is missing, ask — the bridge usually already has the plumbing, it just needs exposing.

Ask the server something

A JObject is just a small JSON-style bundle of values. Use it when one side needs to ask the other side a question.

In this example the client asks whether a feature is unlocked, and the server sends back one value: unlocked.

using CUCoreLib.Networking;
using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq;
using UnityEngine;

private void Awake()
{
    // This runs on the server when a client asks this question.
    MultiplayerApi.RegisterServerHandler("mymod.is-feature-unlocked", request =>
    {
        string featureId = request?.Value<string>("featureId");
        bool unlocked = featureId == "challenge-mode";

        return new JObject
        {
            ["unlocked"] = unlocked
        };
    });
}

private void AskServerIfGlassworksIsUnlocked()
{
    MultiplayerApi.RequestServer(
        "mymod.is-feature-unlocked",
        new JObject
        {
            ["featureId"] = "challenge-mode"
        },
        response =>
        {
            bool unlocked = response?.Value<bool?>("unlocked") ?? false;

            if (unlocked)
            {
                Debug.Log("Challenge mode is unlocked!");
            }
        }
    );
}

RegisterServerHandler answers the question, RequestServer asks it, and JObject is the note passed between them.

For a machine whose mode the host decides, the same pair runs in reverse on the way back: the client requests a change, the server validates it, applies it, and Broadcasts the accepted value to everyone. The editor on the right is exactly that round trip.

Custom snapshot modules

Use MultiplayerApi.RegisterSyncModule when your mod owns shared state that no registry covers: discovered markers, machine recipes, per-world unlocks, cached server decisions. A module is one capture callback and, optionally, one apply callback.

This should look familiar from the Saving API. Same shape, except snapshots cross the network instead of the disk.

using CUCoreLib.Networking;
using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq;

private readonly Dictionary<string, Vector2> markers = new Dictionary<string, Vector2>();

private void Awake()
{
    MultiplayerApi.RegisterSyncModule(
        "glassworks.markers",
        CaptureMarkerSnapshot,
        ApplyMarkerSnapshot
    );
}

private JObject CaptureMarkerSnapshot()
{
    JObject root = new JObject();
    foreach (KeyValuePair<string, Vector2> marker in markers)
    {
        root[marker.Key] = new JObject
        {
            ["x"] = marker.Value.x,
            ["y"] = marker.Value.y
        };
    }

    return root;
}

private void ApplyMarkerSnapshot(JObject snapshot)
{
    if (snapshot == null) return;

    markers.Clear();
    foreach (JProperty property in snapshot.Properties())
    {
        JObject marker = property.Value as JObject;
        if (marker == null) continue;

        markers[property.Name] = new Vector2(
            marker.Value<float?>("x") ?? 0f,
            marker.Value<float?>("y") ?? 0f
        );
    }
}
  • Capture runs on whoever owns the state, at any moment, so keep it cheap and change nothing in it.
  • Apply can run more than once: a snapshot received outside a world is cached and replayed when you load one, and a new session re-pulls it. Clear then refill, like the example above, rather than merging incrementally.
  • Modules apply in one pass, and lootpools is deliberately last because its counts depend on item definitions. Do not rely on any other ordering.
  • Per-player state does not belong in a snapshot module. Snapshots are shared, so one player's capture would overwrite everyone's — use a server handler, or the status API below.

Statuses, per player

Your own custom statuses already sync: every client asks the host for its own body snapshot once a second, and the host answers from the sender's body, so one player's effects can never overwrite another's. No code needed.

Reading somebody else's statuses is a request. Use KrokMP's clientId to choose which player body to read — a clientId is the multiplayer player ID, not the display name.

GetCustomPlayerData returns that player's custom BodyStatus payloads, GetCustomPlayerLimbData their custom LimbStatus payloads, and the Request... pair is the client-side version of the same read.

// Ask the server for one player's custom body statuses.
MultiplayerApi.RequestCustomPlayerData(clientId, response =>
{
    JArray bodyStatuses = response?["body"] as JArray;
    Debug.Log("Body status payloads: " + (bodyStatuses?.Count ?? 0));
});

// Ask the server for one player's custom limb statuses.
MultiplayerApi.RequestCustomPlayerLimbData(clientId, response =>
{
    JArray limbStatuses = response?["limbs"] as JArray;
    Debug.Log("Limb status payloads: " + (limbStatuses?.Count ?? 0));
});

When KrokMP renames something

KrokMP renames members and moves types between releases. NetPlayer.plrcolor in 4.0.1 is NetPlayer.playerColor in 4.1.2, and KrokoshaCasualtiesMP.StatePrinter is now Together.StatePrinter. A mod that hard-codes either spelling gets null from the other build, which usually surfaces as an Object of type X cannot be converted to type Y further down your own code.

ResolveKrokMpType and FindKrokMpMember accept any known spelling and return whatever the running KrokMP actually has, so the same mod binary works on both builds. CUCoreLib keeps the spelling list, and adds to it as KrokMP renames things, so you do not have to.

4.0.14.1.2
NetPlayer.steam_idNetPlayer.SteamId
NetPlayer.plrcolorNetPlayer.playerColor
NetPlayer.additional_profile_tag_iconsNetPlayer.KnownUserTagIcons
KrokoshaCasualtiesMP.KrokoshaCoopModAssetsKrokoshaCasualtiesMP.CoopModAssets
KrokoshaCasualtiesMP.FontUntilsTogether.FontUtils
KrokoshaCasualtiesMP.HingeJointStateTogether.HingeJointState
KrokoshaCasualtiesMP.StatePrinterTogether.StatePrinter
 
using System.Reflection;
using CUCoreLib.Networking;

// Cached once, then used on either KrokMP build. Works for both fields and properties.
private static MemberInfo _playerColorMember;

private static Color24? ReadPlayerColor(object netPlayer)
{
    if (netPlayer == null) return null;

    if (_playerColorMember == null)
    {
        // Either spelling is fine here; both resolve on 4.0.1 and on 4.1.2.
        _playerColorMember = MultiplayerApi.FindKrokMpMember("KrokoshaCasualtiesMP.NetPlayer", "plrcolor");
    }

    return _playerColorMember?.GetValue(netPlayer) as Color24?;
}

FindKrokMpMember takes a Type or a type name, and returns a MemberInfo so fields and properties read the same way. Cache it — the lookup walks every known spelling.

What this cannot fix


If your mod reads the field directly — someNetPlayer.plrcolor — the C# compiler bakes that exact name into your assembly, and KrokMP 4.1.2 throws MissingFieldException when your own IL runs, before any CUCoreLib API is involved. Nothing CUCoreLib can do at load time would rescue that. Switch the call site to FindKrokMpMember as above. Types you declare in your own code that merely reference KrokMP types by name in a field signature have the same problem.

When it does not work

The one health check: with KrokMP installed and CUCoreLib compatible, the log contains CUCoreLib, with friends! during patching. No line, no multiplayer compat.

SymptomUsually
IsAvailable is false with KrokMP installedAn unsupported KrokMP build, or a signature CUCoreLib could not match. It disables the bridge on purpose rather than mis-sending — the log says which receiver it gave up on.
Your content spawns as air, or the wrong itemThe string IDs differ between machines. Every peer needs the same IDs; content-only mods can be missing on a peer, IDs cannot.
Your custom item exists for a peer but does nothingExpected. Definitions cross the wire, your MonoBehaviour logic does not. That peer needs the mod.
Terrain tiles swapped, or a grid-like worldA custom tile index outside 36-255, or peers with different tile tables.
State you changed is missing for clients that already joinedSnapshots are pulled on join. Either BroadcastSnapshot from the host, or send a message.
Everything desyncs, only in some lobbiesMixed KrokMP builds. 4.0.1 and 4.1.2 are not mutually compatible inside KrokMP itself.
Half a module arrives, nothing else brokeYour capture or apply threw. CUCoreLib logs it and carries on: multiplayer snapshot capture failed for module.
Nothing happens on the other sideEither the channel name differs (they are case-sensitive) or the handler was registered after the first message. A handler that throws is logged as multiplayer server handler failed for and swallowed, and if it was a server handler then no response is sent, so the requester's callback never arrives.
CUCoreLib payload exceeds the 16 MiB frame limitToo much in one message. Split it across sends, or move durable state into a sync module.
Registration throws after a hot reloadBy design. Multiplayer channels and sync modules are excluded from strict content reload; restart instead.
